definition.summary: Dense or grouped-query attention, self or cross, with optional window, biases, output gate and Q/K norm.
definition.description:
Projects `input` to `heads` query heads and `kv_heads` key/value heads of `head_dim`, scores each query against the keys its `mask` allows, and projects the weighted values back to `width`. Fewer KV heads than query heads is grouped-query attention; one KV head is multi-query attention.

Three arguments change what the primitive *is* rather than how it computes:

- `cross` makes it **cross-attention**: keys and values come from the `source_values` port, in the stream the edge into it carries, and the cache is frozen once that stream is complete;
- `window` bounds the span a query may attend to, and turns the cache into a ring of that span;
- `streaming` says the input arrives in fragments (§5.3): the cache is carried across fragments even when `mask` is `none`, so a later fragment can attend to earlier ones.

`rope` and `temperature` change the computation, never a tensor or a state, which is why they are not structural; `qk_norm` declares its learned scales inside itself (`qk_norm.scale`), so that a scale cannot be declared without the normalization it belongs to. Each is a closed record or enum, so a variant the contract does not name is refused rather than passed through. The `kv` state exists whenever the computation can be resumed — a causal or chunked mask, a streaming input, or cross-attention. A bidirectional encoder processed in one pass (`mask: none`, neither `streaming` nor `cross`) is stateless.

The projections are stored as the reference implementation stores them — `q`, `k`, `v` and `out`, one tensor each; with `output_gate`, the query projection carries the gate rows interleaved per head (`q_gated`).

width.description: Feature width of `input` and `output`: the residual stream dimension.

head_dim.description: Dimension of one head; queries, keys and values share it.

kv_heads.note: without GQA, as many KV heads as Q heads: a fact of the primitive, hence a contract default
kv_heads.description: Number of key/value heads. Fewer than `heads` is grouped-query attention; one is multi-query attention.

mask.description: Which positions a query may attend to.

value_descriptions.causal: Each position attends to itself and to earlier positions; the cache grows with the sequence.
value_descriptions.chunked: Causal within fixed chunks of `chunk.span` positions; the cache is a ring of one chunk.
value_descriptions.none: Every position attends to every other. Stateless unless `streaming` or `source` says otherwise.

window.description: Sliding window: a query attends to at most `span` preceding positions, and the cache becomes a ring of that span. Inapplicable with `mask: chunked`, whose span is `chunk.span`.

span.description: Chunk span, in tokens: a query attends within its own chunk of `span` positions.

chunk.description: Chunked attention: the positions a query may attend to are its own chunk of `chunk.span` tokens. Required with `mask: chunked`, forbidden otherwise; the cache is a ring of one chunk.

cross.note: keys and values come from another stream; false = self-attention
cross.description: Cross-attention: keys and values come from the value on `source_values`, in the stream that edge carries; the cache grows along that stream and is frozen once it is complete. False, keys and values come from `input`.

streaming.description: The input arrives in fragments (§5.3). The cache is carried across fragments even when `mask` is `none`.

layout.description: How the rotated pairs are laid out along `head_dim`.

value_descriptions.split: Pair channel `i` with `i + rotary/2` over the rotated channels — rotate-half — the Llama and GPT-NeoX layout.
value_descriptions.interleaved: Pair channel `2i` with `2i+1` — the GPT-J layout.
value_descriptions.2d: Two-dimensional rotation over patch rows and columns (vision).

partial.description: Fraction of `head_dim` that is rotated; the rest is left as is. The rotated channels are the first `partial * head_dim` of each head, and their base frequencies are computed on that width, not on `head_dim`. Absent, the whole head is rotated.

sections.description: How the three sections sit on the rotated frequency axis: `contiguous` — all temporal frequencies, then height, then width (Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL); `interleaved` — temporal, height and width frequencies alternating (Qwen3-VL, Qwen 3.5, Qwen 3.8). Two published layouts, so no default: a document says which. For a single position stream they compute the same thing; an image tells them apart.

value_descriptions.contiguous: Sections laid end to end: `t` temporal frequencies, then `h`, then `w`.
value_descriptions.interleaved: Sections interleaved frequency by frequency: temporal, height, width, temporal, …

mrope.description: Multimodal rotary: the rotated channels are split into temporal, height and width sections, each driven by its own position index; `sections` says how the three are laid out on the frequency axis.

kind.description: Context-extension method applied to the rotary frequencies.

value_descriptions.yarn: YaRN: per-frequency interpolation between `beta_fast` and `beta_slow` wavelengths; the rotated queries and keys are multiplied by `attention_factor`.
value_descriptions.llama3: Llama 3 frequency scaling: wavelengths above `orig_ctx/low` are scaled by `factor`, below `orig_ctx/high` are kept, in between interpolated.
value_descriptions.linear: Position interpolation: every position is divided by `factor`.

factor.description: Ratio between the served context and `orig_ctx`.

orig_ctx.description: Context length the frequencies were trained at.

beta_fast.description: YaRN: number of rotations above which a frequency is left unscaled.

beta_slow.description: YaRN: number of rotations below which a frequency is fully interpolated.

attention_factor.description: YaRN: the factor multiplying the rotated queries and keys — the paper's 0.1·ln(factor) + 1 unless the checkpoint defines otherwise (Ministral 3: 1).

scaling.description: Context-extension scaling of the rotary frequencies; absent, the frequencies are used as trained. A kind's fields are all required under it: the published values differ, so none is defaulted.

rope.description: Rotary position encoding: base, layout, rotated fraction, multimodal sections and context-extension scaling. Changes the computation, not a tensor or a state.

eps.description: Added to the mean square (`rms`) or the variance (`layer`) before the root; changes no tensor.

zero_centered.description: The scales are stored as offsets from one: the scale applied is `1 + q_norm` and `1 + k_norm`, as Qwen 3.5 stores them. Changes no tensor.

scale.note: present: the Q/K norm has learned scales, q_norm and k_norm
scale.description: The normalization has a learned per-channel scale: present, this record declares the `q_norm` and `k_norm` slots; an empty record is a plain scale. Absent, queries and keys are normalized without a scale.

qk_norm.description: Normalization applied to the projected queries and keys, per head over `head_dim`, before the rotary embedding. Its learned scale, when there is one, is declared inside it: a scale cannot be declared without the normalization it belongs to. Absent, queries and keys are not normalized.

floor.description: Positions per temperature step: the scale grows once per `floor` positions.

scale.description: Growth of the logit scale per step.

temperature.description: Position-dependent attention temperature: the logits of position `p` are multiplied by `1 + scale * log(1 + p / floor)`.

q_bias.note: learned Q bias; a synthetic runtime zero stays false
q_bias.description: Learned bias on the query projection.

k_bias.note: learned K bias; a synthetic runtime zero stays false
k_bias.description: Learned bias on the key projection.

v_bias.description: Learned bias on the value projection.

out_bias.description: Learned bias on the output projection.

output_gate.note: per-head sigmoid gate; its rows live in the gated query projection q_gated
output_gate.description: Per-head sigmoid gate on the attention output, computed from `input` by the gate rows of the gated query projection `q_gated`.

input.description: Residual-stream activation: one vector of `width` per element of the indexing domain.

source_values.note: cross-attention: K/V come from ANOTHER stream, the one the edge into this port carries (an `align` transform).
source_values.description: Values of the cross-attention source, in the stream of the edge that feeds this port.

output.description: Attention output after the output projection and the gate, if any, in the domain of `input`.

q.description: Query projection: `heads` heads of `head_dim` rows, stored as the reference implementation stores it.

q_gated.description: Gated query projection: per head, `head_dim` query rows then `head_dim` gate rows, as the reference implementation stores them; the gate rows are applied through a sigmoid to the attention output.

out.description: Output projection from the concatenated query heads back to `width`.

q_norm.description: Learned scale of the query normalization.

k_norm.description: Learned scale of the key normalization.

k.description: Keys of one position: one `head_dim` vector per KV head.

v.description: Values of one position, same layout as `k`.

carried_across.description: With `streaming`, the cache survives between the invocations that deliver successive fragments of the input's stream, whatever the mask.

append.description: Write the keys and values of a new position at the end.

read.description: Read every cached position for a query.

rules.description: Bidirectional streaming encoder: fragments accumulate; the port-level carrying condition keeps the cache across fragments.
Cross-attention: indexed by the stream of `source_values`, frozen once that stream is complete.
Sliding window: a ring of `window.span` positions.
Plain causal decoding: append per position.

kv.description: Keys and values of every position the current query may still attend to: two components of one shape. Which law applies is decided by the first matching rule below.

partitions.description: Tensor parallelism across query heads; the output projection needs an all-reduce.
Partition across KV heads, only when there is more than one.

partitions.note: KV payload partition by head: target tagged payload, not argument
partitions.description: The cache itself partitions by KV head, with no communication.

domain_transforms.note: cross-attention: K/V come from another stream (§5.3). The output stays in the query domain; attention aligns the source onto it.
domain_transforms.description: Cross-attention aligns the source domain onto the query domain.

definition.note: Dense or grouped Q/K/V attention, with bias, output gate and Q/K normalization variants.

logical_cost.description: Scores and weighted values of every query head against one cached position.
